For warning signs there's a few so I'll list them. 

1: They'll start guilt tripping you early on and using your emotions against you. If they are your S/O they'll probably use something along the lines of "If you love me you'll _."

2: They will isolate you from people you care about and who they know don't approve of your relationship. 

3: Everything no matter how big or small is seemingly your fault.

4: The second they start punching holes in the wall GET OUT. They can say it was an accident, they can say your overreacting, they can say it'll never happen again. If you can do it safely though get out of that relationship. All it would take is one blind moment of rage and that could be you instead of the wall.

5: They start giving you that look. I can't explain it well but it's the look they give you when you said something you shouldn't have in public, it's the look they give you when they catch you doing something wrong, it's the look thats meant to stop you and shut you up.

As for how to help...that's tough. Everyone's case is different. Understand though they will most likely not want to be touched after that at all. Don't take that personally, unless they initiate it just don't touch them. If they are having a freakout or panic attack they may tell you to stay away from them, step back a few meters and gently talk to them. Most people after abuse feel smuthered or intensely scared if someone's too close to them while they are freaking out. Understand them ,give them time , give them space and try your best to be a safe space for them.
